observation_summary: The compiler performs an aggressive optimization that changes the semantic behavior of the code, specifically regarding the evaluation order of expressions involving side effects.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the compiler's function inliner performs direct inlining of function calls without considering that the function body might have side effects that interact with the arguments. Specifically, if a function body contains side effects (e.g., modifying a property) and the arguments passed to the function can also be side-effected, the inlining process can change the evaluation order or the state of the arguments, leading to incorrect program behavior. The fix introduces a check to verify if the function body has side effects and, if so, prevents inlining if any of the arguments are susceptible to being side-effected.
